key_insight: Sharing coefficients can be turned from a billing tool into day-ahead price signals that steer household demand toward using local PV and cutting feeder reverse power flow.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives energy community managers a network-aware demand response mechanism that improves local solar self-consumption while reducing low-voltage feeder stress.
method: Iteratively forecast demand and PV, then compute proportional sharing coefficients for each household.
Convert allocated shared energy into household-specific price signals for demand reshaping via convex optimization.
Compare feeder-aware sharing within each feeder against feeder-agnostic sharing through a single community pool.
evidence_signal: Using measured profiles from 15 households with AC power flow analysis, the method reduced feeder reverse energy by up to 45.0% and 44.6% on selected days and by 69.0% and 66.3% over the annual window.
watch_item: Real-world deployment depends on accurate PV/load forecasts and household participation, since the control signal assumes users respond to price incentives.
paper_title: Sharing Coefficient-Based Price Signals for Demand Response in Renewable Energy Communities
